**The document does not report HumanEval results.** HumanEval does not appear anywhere in the paper, so there is no pass@1 retention figure for Qwen3 14B→32B or any other pair.

**What the paper evaluates**

- **Main benchmarks:** ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, MMLU 5-shot, GSM8K 8-shot with chain-of-thought, and WikiText-2 perplexity (p. 6; Table 11, p. 16).
- **Multi-turn:** CoQA (p. 6, p. 8).
- **Held-out benchmarks:** PIQA, BoolQ and ARC-Easy (p. 21).
- **Calibration-domain sweep:** also adds ARC-Easy, PIQA and BoolQ (p. 15).

The only code-related item is CodeAlpaca, which is used as an alternative *calibration* corpus, not as an evaluation benchmark. On Qwen3 14B→32B it lowers HellaSwag by 5.24 pp compared with FineWeb-Edu calibration (Table 8, p. 15).

**Reported retention for Qwen3 14B→32B (ridge, k=8)**

| Benchmark | Retention | Source |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (the only generation benchmark) | 95.6% | Table 1, p. 6 |
| ARC-C | 101.0% | Table 1, p. 6 |
| HellaSwag | 97.6% | Table 1, p. 6 |
| WinoGrande | 98.5% | Table 1, p. 6 |
| MMLU | 95.0% | Table 1, p. 6 |
| Average | 97.6% (96.3% floor-normalized) | Table 1, p. 6 |
| PIQA (held out) | 98.0% | Table 18, p. 21 |
| BoolQ (held out) | 101.9% | Table 18, p. 21 |
| ARC-Easy (held out) | 99.8% | Table 18, p. 21 |

Code-generation performance such as HellaEval would need to be measured separately; the paper gives no basis for estimating it.
